header.stance: 實質殖利率上升，大額公司債供給增加壓力

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價反彈與Amazon供給推升美債殖利率

荷莫茲海峽商船再遭攻擊，油價反彈，加上Amazon發行$250億債券，美債週二回吐前一天的小幅漲勢。10年期殖利率上升7個基點至4.55%，30年期上升6個基點至5.05%。各天期普遍承壓，殖利率升幅主要來自實質利率，通膨補償僅小幅增加。

市場原本期待能源降價減輕Fed的通膨壓力，這項支撐如今出現變數。紐約Fed的6月調查也顯示，家庭對未來一年與三年的通膨預期上升，儘管受訪者預期汽油漲幅放緩。醫療與租金帶來的物價壓力，早在週二油價反彈前便已存在。貿易逆差擴大雖不利成長，仍不足以抵銷能源與債券供給對美債的壓力。

Amazon順利完成融資，但隨最終定價利差收窄，訂單明顯縮減；接連承接大型雲端業者發債之後，投資人對價格愈來愈敏感。美國3年期公債標售則有強勁的投資人需求，交易商承接比例創新低。買盤並未消失，卻愈來愈挑天期、發行人與價格。

## 實質殖利率全面上升，3年期標售仍有強勁買盤

2年期殖利率上升6個基點至4.19%，5年期上升6個基點至4.27%，30年期也上升6個基點至5.05%。10年期多升1個基點，使2年與10年期利差擴大至36個基點，2年與30年期利差則維持86個基點。曲線大致平行上移，斜率變化不大；若拉長至一週，長端壓力仍較明顯，2、5、10及30年期累計升幅分別為5、8、11及14個基點。

10年期實質殖利率升6個基點至2.30%，損益兩平通膨率升1至2.25%。5、7及20年期實質殖利率升5、6、6個基點至1.99%、2.14%、2.65%，30年期升5至2.84%。通膨不確定性回升，但可觀察的通膨補償增幅仍遠小於實質殖利率。

荷莫茲商船遭攻擊、美國撤銷允許伊朗石油銷售的豁免，使WTI盤中最多上漲5.8%。近期能源降價可能停頓的風險重現，尚不能據此認定更大的月跌幅已永久反轉。

消費者調查增加另一項疑慮。一年通膨預期由3.5%升至3.7%，三年由3.1%升至3.3%、為2022年6月以來最高，五年維持3%。家庭預期汽油及食品漲幅較低，醫療與租金卻更高，因此不只是對當日原油的反應。

John Williams表示，能源降價應有助於未來幾個月的整體通膨回落，目前政策位置合宜。不過，前景仍有不確定性，Fed也已在6月聲明中移除明確利率指引。利率交換市場反映年底前約32個基點的升息幅度，部分投資人則買進選擇權，押注升息預期減弱，甚至政策轉向降息。市場的主要定價仍偏緊，交易部位卻保留了另一種可能。

5月貿易對成長較不利。商品與服務逆差由修正後$546億擴至$776億，出口降3.2%至$3,177億，進口升3.3%至$3,953億；實質商品逆差增18.7%至$1,000億，削弱第二季淨出口貢獻。能源與供給主導之下，這項拖累未帶來債券反彈。

### 較高殖利率吸引公債買方

$580億3年期標售得標殖利率4.179%，低於截止時發行前交易的4.185%，交易商僅取得7.7%、創該天期最低。殖利率上升後有投資人承接，但整體市場仍承壓，10年與30年標售尚待進行。

財政部另售約$520億364天期，最高利率3.860%、投標倍數3.14，間接、直接與交易商承接60.13%、4.56%、35.31%。約$900億42天期為3.635%、投標倍數2.74，承接63.51%、2.70%、33.79%，兩券7月9日交割。

次級一年期殖利率跳升11個基點至4.05%，6週期升5至3.71%，4週期降2至3.65%，8週期維持3.72%。13週期降1至3.82%，17週期維持3.87%，26週期升1至3.96%。較長國庫券比最短現金天期更明顯反映政策重估。

## Amazon完成巨額發債，訂單卻隨利差收緊縮減

Amazon發行$250億債券，分八個券種、天期介於3至40年，完成2026年的美元融資需求。資金可用於償債、收購、資本支出及其他一般企業用途，最長券2066年到期。本週市場除了美國公債標售，還得承接這批大額長天期公司債。

訂單高峰$620億，銀行調低最終利差後降至約$410億，約為發行額1.6倍，低於今年美國投資級平均約四倍。最長券利差收緊20個基點後，以美債加約125個基點定價，讓利仍為近月常見程度的數倍。交易進行時，既有科技債也走弱。

Amazon仍有能力大額籌資，但買方不再照單全收。過去一年，公司累計發債約$1,070億，包括3月的$370億與€145億債券，以及其後的瑞郎、加幣借款；今年預期支出接近$2,000億。最新統計顯示，全球2026年AI相關債券供給已達約$3,350億，超過2025年的兩倍。

市場先前已承接Nvidia與SpaceX在6月各發行的$250億債券。SpaceX定價後的次級市場跌勢說明，初始訂單龐大，不代表後續價格穩定。如今Amazon訂單隨利差收窄而縮減，再度顯示投資人對持債集中度與長天期風險有所顧慮。

LQD跌0.73%，HYG跌0.14%，JNK跌0.10%。投資級較大跌幅伴隨指標殖利率上升，高收益跌幅有限，並非全面撤離信用。

### 再融資可爭取時間，不能替代流失現金

Lazard表示，Nouryon、CABB、Lanxess及Ineos等歐洲化工業者，趁衝突期間資本市場仍有流動性，辦理再融資、延後債務到期。但需求疲弱、能源成本高昂及產能過剩的問題未解，融資窗口也開始收窄。近30%的德國化工公司反映原料短缺，使原本就疲弱的營運再添壓力。

Getty Images與Shutterstock合併告吹後，財務困境更加迫切。標普將其評等由B降至CCC+，認為目前的資本結構難以維持。交易失敗使原本預期的$1.62億現金效益落空，每年債務支出卻仍約$8,600萬。面對逾$19億債務，債權人開始聯合行動；公司$1.5億循環信貸額度僅剩$3,000萬可動用。

歐洲央行則準備將氣候不確定性評分納入公司債擔保品管理。高污染、或缺乏可信轉型計畫的發行人，其債券作為擔保品時可能被打更大的折扣。由於銀行向央行借款、以及使用公司債擔保的規模都偏低，初期影響預料有限，但長期可能拉開發行人之間的融資成本。

## 日本標售漲勢消退，所得成長支持正常化

日本30年期首次4%票息，吸引投標倍數4.55，為2019年以來最高，高於前次2.94及一年平均3.41。殖利率一度降7個基點，數小時內漲勢卻反轉。高殖利率有強勁投標，仍未解決財政、日圓及升息步調疑慮。

政府截至2041年3月的¥370兆投資路徑，以及以債務占GDP為主要指標的取向，使名目成長與融資假設受關注。本地殖利率提高可改變日本機構與海外債的比較，成功標售本身卻不能證明配置已持續轉變。

5月名目現金薪資年增3.2%，前月修正3.6%，連續第四個月至少3%，為1992年以來最長，整體仍低於經濟學家預估。底薪增3%，排除獎金及加班的較穩定全職指標增2.4%，實質薪資增1.4%、連續第五個月上升。

日本央行實質消費活動指數增0.6%，耐久財增1.2%、非耐久0.9%、服務0.2%。這些實際所得與消費，接續假日已報導的強勁工會協商，為薪資物價循環提供比談判結果更直接的依據。

經濟成長戰略大臣城內實否認政府有意將利率壓在不合理的低檔，並指出政府曾參與將政策利率提高至1%的會議。市場因此更關注年底前再次升息的可能；政府龐大的投資計畫，則仍需資金支持。

德國5月工業生產增0.9%，汽車增3.6%領先，年變化持平；資本與消費財改善，中間財降0.4%。ECB委員Fabio Panetta仍認為前景脆弱，上行通膨與下行成長風險並存，支持6月升息後避免預定路徑，也區分目前供給衝擊與2022年的情況。

### 義大利找到美元需求，英國面對長期財政算術

義大利5、10及30年期美元債籌$60億、訂單近$200億，偏重短天期。10年期對德利差約77個基點，低於Giorgia Meloni上任時約250。資金仍可取得，但2026年中長期發債計畫€3,500億至€3,650億，供給仍大。

英國財政監督機構估計，2031至2032年度起要把債務穩在目前GDP 95%附近，每年需約£1,000億持續增稅或減支，約當預估境內公司稅收入；若回到金融危機前40%，還需另£1,500億整頓。不變政策下，國防成本上升、燃油稅減少，可使2075至2076年度債務達GDP 300%。這是長期情境，非政府眼前須支付的現金。

中國則擴大離岸人民幣融資管道。香港人民幣業務融資安排的規模將增加逾一倍至人民幣5,000億元，南向債券通年度額度也由人民幣5,000億元提高至8,000億元。更多離岸流動性、加上境內投資人購買境外債券的額度增加，有助於擴大區域資金流動，但美日仍各自面對債券供給壓力。

## 巴西維持本地流動性，Codelco債務負擔加重

巴西R$2.3兆通膨連結債市場，實質殖利率逼近8%，財政與需求變化使流動性緊張。財政部已減量、取消標售，官員保留買回選項。調整供給與動用現金可緩解失衡，也顯示控制通膨之際融通較高支出的困難。

重返歐元債市場之後，巴西另準備發行首筆熊貓債，規模最高人民幣50億元、約$7.36億；今年累計已在國際市場籌得約$100億。官員表示，目的在於分散投資人來源，並為巴西企業建立定價參考，而非本地融資受阻。目前外幣債約占聯邦債務4%，年度計畫目標為7%；即使達標，本幣債務占比仍超過90%。

智利Codelco雖有AI銅需求前景，營運卻有問題。負債約$250億，其中國際債逾$200億，產量在28年低點，成本比全球三大礦商平均高逾50%。內部檢查發現2025年產量高估近2.7萬公噸、約2%。銅稀缺支持戰略價值及潛在收入，智利本身債務與赤字提高，卻限制支應下一輪資本支出或承接營運落差的能力。

中國6月外匯存底減少$260億、降幅0.75%，至$3.4163兆。官方指出，美元升值帶來的匯率換算、以及資產價格漲跌，影響了存底估值；這項數字本身不足以證明央行干預或資本外流，也不宜與新公布的離岸人民幣融資安排混為一談。

菲律賓6月通膨實際6.4%，低於前月6.8%及先前預估6.5%；核心卻加速至4.4%，為2023年12月以來最高，使央行仍保留再行動選項。披索小升，但通膨仍超過3%目標兩倍。

美元指數上漲0.29%至101.14，加上美債殖利率升高，EMB下跌0.43%。外部金融環境收緊之餘，各國仍有不同的壓力來源：巴西面對本地通膨連結債流動性問題，Codelco需要支應投資的資金，中國存底受估值影響，菲律賓則仍須抑制國內通膨。

## 能源跳升，科技與黃金轉弱

荷莫茲航運威脅回升，WTI收漲2.76%至$70.44，布蘭特漲3.01%至$74.16，美元也升、美債卻跌。這不同於一般地緣避險流入名目政府債的行情：能源風險伴隨實質殖利率及供給提高。

S&P 500跌0.45%，Nasdaq 100跌1.77%，半導體跌4.65%。AI支出及估值疑問與Amazon融資同時出現，使股市下跌連結到建設借款規模。大盤及高收益較小跌幅，仍未顯示全面撤資。

VIX升3.60%至16.13，相對半導體跌勢仍有限。地緣緊張下黃金卻跌0.24%至$4,145.30，較高實質殖利率及美元對不生息資產不利；前月大跌後，金價仍高於$4,000。

原油比一個月前仍低很多，WTI跌22.20%、布蘭特跌20.34%。週二重新打開通膨風險，尚未證明整體能源下降已結束。這關係Williams的通膨放緩預期，也攸關防範Fed緊縮減少的避險部位。

## Fed紀錄與長債標售檢驗重估

6月16日至17日FOMC會議紀錄將於7月8日美東14:00公布，接著是7月9日08:30的失業救濟金申請、以及7月14日08:30的6月CPI。委員對政策的看法、勞動市場變化，以及整體、核心與住宅通膨細項，將有助於判斷油價反彈究竟是短期擾動，還是持續的政策壓力。部分選擇權部位則押注升息幅度減少，反映投資人仍在為不同結果布局。

財政部將於7月8日13:00增額發行$390億、票息4.375%的10年期公債，7月9日13:00再增額發行$220億、票息5.000%的30年期公債，兩券均於7月15日交割。3年期標售需求強勁，Amazon訂單卻對價格敏感；接下來長債的得標殖利率相對發行前交易水準、各類買方得標比例，以及標售後走勢，將進一步呈現長天期需求的強弱。

海外方面，紐西蘭央行將於7月7日美東22:00公布決策，中國6月CPI與PPI於7月8日21:30公布；日本央行區域評估及約¥2.5兆的5年期公債標售，則安排在7月9日東京交易時段。各地的物價與投標結果，將為政策及債市比較提供更具體的依據。

overall_summary.headline: 油價反彈，Amazon巨額發債考驗債券買盤
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷莫茲海峽航運再遭攻擊，油價回升，加上Amazon發行$250億債券，美債回吐週一漲勢。10年期殖利率上升7個基點至4.55%，其中實質殖利率貢獻6個基點。家庭通膨預期也上升，貿易逆差擴大則釋出較弱的成長訊號。

Amazon的訂單隨定價利差收窄，由$620億降至約$410億，認購倍數約1.6倍，低於投資級平均約四倍。相對地，$580億3年期美債標售得標殖利率低於發行前交易水準，交易商僅承接7.7%、創新低。市場仍有買盤，但價格與天期愈來愈重要。

日本30年期新券票息首度達4%，標售後漲勢卻未能延續。巴西實質殖利率逼近8%，財政部減少本地通膨連結債供給；Codelco則在銅需求前景之外，面對低產量與高負債的投資難題。接下來將公布Fed會議紀錄，並進行10年與30年期美債標售。
overall_summary.summary: 10年期美債殖利率上升7個基點至4.55%，主要來自實質利率。Amazon完成$250億發債，但訂單隨利差收窄而縮減；3年期公債標售需求則依然強勁。

section_summaries.section_title: 油價反彈與Amazon供給推升美債殖利率
section_summaries.summary: 能源風險再起，加上Amazon發債，美債回吐漲勢；實質利率主導殖利率升幅，公司債與公債標售需求卻明顯不同。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil's Rebound and Amazon Supply Send Treasury Yields Higher

Treasuries reversed Monday's modest rally as renewed Hormuz attacks lifted oil and Amazon brought another $25 billion of debt to market. The 10-year yield rose 7 basis points to 4.55%, while the 30-year added 6 to 5.05%. Losses extended across the curve, with real yields accounting for most of the move rather than a large jump in inflation compensation.

The energy reversal challenged a source of recent policy relief. Household inflation expectations also rose at one and three years in the New York Fed's June survey, although respondents had anticipated less gasoline inflation. Medical and rent costs were part of the persistence even before Tuesday's oil move. A wider trade deficit offered a softer growth signal but did not outweigh the pressure from energy and issuance.

Amazon completed its financing, yet its orderbook shrank markedly as final spreads tightened. The result exposed price sensitivity in a market absorbing repeated hyperscaler deals. By contrast, Treasury's three-year auction drew strong end-investor demand and left dealers a record-low share. Buyers had not abandoned debt; they were demanding different compensation depending on the maturity and issuer.

## Real Yields Rise Across the Curve Despite Strong Three-Year Bidding

Two-year yields rose 6 basis points to 4.19%, five years added 6 to 4.27% and 30 years gained 6 to 5.05%. The 10-year's 7-basis-point increase widened 2s10s by just 1 to 36, while 2s30s held at 86. This was a broadly parallel selloff rather than another major change in slope. Weekly increases remained larger farther out: 5, 8, 11 and 14 basis points at two, five, 10 and 30 years.

At 10 years, real yield rose 6 basis points to 2.30% and breakeven inflation increased 1 to 2.25%. Five-, seven- and 20-year real yields rose 5, 6 and 6 basis points to 1.99%, 2.14% and 2.65%; 30 years added 5 to 2.84%. Inflation uncertainty had returned, but the measured increase in benchmark compensation for inflation was small beside the rise in real yields.

Attacks on commercial vessels in Hormuz and the US withdrawal of a waiver allowing Iranian oil sales pushed WTI as much as 5.8% higher intraday. The threat reopened the possibility that the recent energy decline would stall. It did not yet establish that oil's much larger monthly fall had permanently reversed.

The consumer survey added a separate concern. One-year inflation expectations rose to 3.7% from 3.5%, and three-year expectations to 3.3% from 3.1%, the highest since June 2022. Five years held at 3%. Respondents expected less gasoline and slightly less food inflation, but more pressure in medical care and rent. The underlying mix was therefore broader than a contemporaneous reaction to crude.

John Williams said falling energy prices should lower overall inflation in coming months and described policy as well positioned. He retained uncertainty and the Fed's decision to remove explicit rate guidance from its June statement. Swaps priced about 32 basis points of tightening by year-end, while some investors bought option structures that would benefit if hike expectations faded or policy eventually turned toward cuts. A restrictive central outlook still left demand for protection against a different outcome.

May trade was weaker for growth. The goods-and-services deficit widened to $77.6 billion from a revised $54.6 billion, as exports fell 3.2% to $317.7 billion and imports rose 3.3% to $395.3 billion. The real-goods deficit increased 18.7% to $100.0 billion, worsening the second-quarter net-export contribution. That drag failed to produce a bond rally in a session dominated by energy and supply.

### Higher Yields Attract Treasury Buyers

The $58 billion three-year auction stopped at 4.179%, below the 4.185% when-issued yield at the bidding deadline. Dealers took 7.7%, a record low for the maturity. Investors absorbed the offering after yields rose, even as the broader market remained under pressure and the 10- and 30-year auctions were still ahead.

Treasury also sold about $52 billion of 364-day bills at 3.860%, with 3.14 bid-to-cover. Indirect, direct and dealer allocations were 60.13%, 4.56% and 35.31%. The roughly $90 billion 42-day sale cleared at 3.635%, with 2.74 coverage and allocations of 63.51%, 2.70% and 33.79%. Both settle July 9.

Secondary one-year bill yields jumped 11 basis points to 4.05%. Six weeks rose 5 to 3.71%, while four weeks fell 2 to 3.65% and eight weeks held at 3.72%. Thirteen weeks eased 1 to 3.82%, 17 weeks held at 3.87% and 26 weeks rose 1 to 3.96%. The outer bill sector joined the policy repricing more forcefully than the shortest cash maturities.

## Amazon Completes a Jumbo Deal as Its Orderbook Shrinks

Amazon sold $25 billion across eight maturities from three to 40 years, completing its US dollar funding needs for 2026. Proceeds could fund debt repayment, acquisitions and capital expenditure among general corporate purposes. The final tranche matured in 2066, placing another large block of long corporate duration alongside the week's Treasury supply.

Orders peaked at $62 billion and fell to about $41 billion as banks reduced the final spreads. At roughly 1.6 times the issue, coverage was well below the year's average near four times for US high-grade deals. The longest tranche priced around 125 basis points over Treasuries after tightening 20 basis points, yet concessions were still several times those commonly seen in recent months. Outstanding technology debt weakened while the sale progressed.

The company retained access on a huge scale, but demand was no longer insensitive to price. The deal took Amazon's issuance over the preceding year to about $107 billion, including March sales of $37 billion in dollars and €14.5 billion in euros and subsequent Swiss-franc and Canadian-dollar borrowing. Expected spending approached $200 billion this year. The latest global tally put 2026 AI-linked bond supply at about $335 billion, more than twice 2025 volume.

Nvidia and SpaceX's $25 billion June transactions were part of that existing supply base, not fresh deals on Tuesday. SpaceX's earlier secondary losses had already shown that large initial books did not guarantee stable post-pricing returns. Amazon's book reduction added direct evidence of investor resistance as another issuer asked portfolios to take concentration and long maturity at tighter spreads.

LQD fell 0.73%, compared with HYG's 0.14% and JNK's 0.10%. The larger investment-grade loss accompanied rising benchmark yields; the relatively small high-yield declines did not resemble an indiscriminate exit from credit.

### Refinancing Buys Time, but Cannot Replace Lost Cash

Lazard said European chemical producers including Nouryon, CABB, Lanxess and Ineos had used the liquidity available during the conflict to extend maturities despite weak demand, high energy costs and excess capacity. That opportunity was beginning to narrow. Nearly 30% of German chemical companies reported material shortages, adding an operating constraint to an already difficult demand environment.

Getty Images faced a more advanced balance-sheet problem after the Shutterstock merger was abandoned. S&P cut its rating to CCC+ from B and called the capital structure unsustainable: the failed transaction removed an expected $162 million cash benefit, while annual debt service remained about $86 million. Lenders organized around more than $1.9 billion of debt, with only $30 million available on a $150 million revolver.

ECB collateral policy introduced a slower-moving distinction. Climate-uncertainty scores for corporate collateral could lead to larger valuation haircuts for heavy polluters and issuers without credible transition plans. Initial effects were expected to be limited because bank borrowing and use of corporate collateral were low. The framework could nevertheless alter relative funding costs over time without constituting an immediate broad liquidity shock.

## Japan's Auction Rally Fades as Income Growth Supports Normalization

Japan's first 4% coupon on a 30-year issue drew 4.55 bid-to-cover, the highest since 2019, up from 2.94 previously and above the 3.41 one-year average. The yield initially fell as much as 7 basis points, but reversed that rally within hours. Strong bidding at high yields had not settled concerns about fiscal plans, the weak yen and the pace of BOJ tightening.

The government's ¥370 trillion investment roadmap through March 2041 and its emphasis on debt-to-GDP kept nominal-growth and financing assumptions in focus. Higher domestic yields could alter Japanese institutions' comparisons with overseas bonds, though a successful auction alone could not establish a durable change in their allocations.

May nominal cash earnings rose 3.2% from a year earlier after a revised 3.6% increase. It was the fourth month at or above 3%, the longest such run since 1992, though the headline missed economists' estimate. Base pay rose 3%, and a less volatile full-time measure excluding bonuses and overtime increased 2.4%. Real earnings gained 1.4%, a fifth consecutive increase.

The BOJ's real Consumption Activity Index rose 0.6%, comprising gains of 1.2% in durables, 0.9% in non-durables and 0.2% in services. These realized income and spending gains followed the strong union settlement already reported over the holiday. They provided a firmer basis for the wage-price argument than negotiations alone.

Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi rejected the suggestion that the government wanted artificially low rates, noting its participation in the meeting that lifted policy to 1%. The statement increased attention on another move by year-end. It did not remove the financing demands of the government's investment agenda.

German industrial production rose 0.9% in May, led by a 3.6% automotive gain; annual production was flat. Capital and consumer goods improved, while intermediate goods fell 0.4%. ECB member Fabio Panetta still described a fragile outlook, with upside inflation and downside growth risks. He defended avoiding a predetermined path after June's hike and distinguished the current supply shock from 2022.

### Italy Finds Dollar Demand; Britain Faces Long-Run Arithmetic

Italy raised $6 billion in five-, 10- and 30-year dollar benchmarks with nearly $20 billion of orders, concentrated in shorter maturities. Its 10-year spread to Germany was about 77 basis points, down from roughly 250 when Giorgia Meloni took office. Access remained strong, although planned medium- and long-term issuance of €350 billion–€365 billion in 2026 kept supply substantial.

The UK fiscal watchdog estimated that stabilizing debt near its current 95% of GDP from 2031–32 would require recurring tax increases or spending cuts of roughly £100 billion annually, comparable with projected onshore corporation-tax receipts. Returning toward the pre-crisis 40% ratio would require another £150 billion. Under unchanged policy, debt could reach 300% of GDP by 2075–76 as defense spending rose and fuel-duty revenue fell. These were long-run scenarios, not an immediate cash call on the government.

China expanded an alternative funding pool. Hong Kong's RMB Business Facility would more than double to 500 billion yuan, and the annual Southbound Bond Connect quota would rise to 800 billion from 500 billion. More offshore yuan liquidity and capacity for mainland investors to buy offshore debt could broaden regional flows, without resolving the separate supply issues in Japan or the US.

## Brazil Defends Local Liquidity as Codelco's Debt Burden Grows

Brazil's real yields approached 8% in a R$2.3 trillion inflation-linked market as fiscal concerns and changing demand strained liquidity. The Treasury had reduced auction sizes and canceled sales; officials kept buybacks available if those measures failed to restore balance. Changing supply and using cash could relieve dislocation, but the intervention also showed the difficulty of financing higher spending while trying to contain inflation.

Brazil was separately preparing an inaugural Panda issue of up to CNY5 billion, about $736 million, after returning to euros. It had raised roughly $10 billion internationally during the year. Officials described diversification and pricing references for Brazilian companies as the purpose, not an inability to fund domestically. Foreign-currency liabilities were about 4% of federal debt against a 7% annual-plan target; more than 90% would remain local-currency even at that target.

Chile's Codelco faced operating problems despite the AI-linked outlook for copper demand. It carried about $25 billion of debt, over $20 billion in international bonds, with output at a 28-year low. Production costs exceeded the average of the three largest global miners by more than 50%. An internal review found 2025 production overstated by almost 27,000 metric tons, about 2%. Copper scarcity supported strategic value and potential revenue, but Chile's rising public debt and deficits limited its ability to finance another investment cycle or absorb underperformance.

China's reserves fell $26.0 billion, or 0.75%, in June to $3.4163 trillion. Officials attributed the decline to currency translation and mixed asset-price moves as the dollar strengthened. That explanation did not establish intervention or capital flight. The reserve valuation change was distinct from the new offshore renminbi facilities.

Philippine June inflation was released at 6.4%, down from 6.8% and slightly below the preceding 6.5% forecast. Core accelerated to 4.4%, its highest since December 2023, leaving the BSP open to further action despite headline relief. The peso gained modestly, but inflation remained more than twice the 3% target.

EMB fell 0.43% as DXY rose 0.29% to 101.14 and Treasury yields increased. That common pressure reached very different balance sheets: Brazil's local inflation-linked market, Codelco's debt-funded investment needs, China's valuation-sensitive reserves and the Philippines' persistent domestic prices.

## Energy Jumps While Technology and Gold Weaken

WTI ended up 2.76% at $70.44 and Brent gained 3.01% to $74.16 after threats to Hormuz traffic returned. The dollar also rose, while Treasuries fell. The combination was unlike a conventional geopolitical flight into nominal government bonds: the renewed energy risk arrived with higher real yields and large issuance.

The S&P 500 declined 0.45%, Nasdaq 100 lost 1.77% and semiconductors fell 4.65%. Questions about AI spending and valuations coincided with Amazon's financing, linking an equity selloff to the scale of borrowing behind the buildout. The smaller broad-index loss and modest high-yield decline did not show an economy-wide liquidation.

VIX rose 3.60% to 16.13, a contained level beside the semiconductor move. Gold fell 0.24% to $4,145.30 despite geopolitical tension, as higher real yields and dollar strength worked against the non-yielding asset. It remained above $4,000 after the previous month's sharp decline.

Oil still stood well below a month earlier: WTI was down 22.20% and Brent 20.34%. Tuesday reopened an inflation risk without yet proving that the broader energy decline had ended. The distinction mattered to both Williams' expectation of lower inflation and the hedges against further Fed tightening.

## Fed Minutes and Long Auctions Test the Repricing

The June 16–17 FOMC minutes arrive July 8 at 14:00 ET, followed by claims July 9 at 08:30 and June CPI July 14 at 08:30. Committee views, labor flows and the headline, core and shelter detail will help distinguish a temporary oil reversal from persistent pressure on policy. The option positions benefiting from less tightening remain a reminder that investors are protecting against more than one outcome.

Treasury reopens $39 billion of the 4.375% 10-year note July 8 at 13:00 ET and $22 billion of the 5.000% 30-year bond July 9 at 13:00; both settle July 15. Stops versus when-issued yields, bidder awards and subsequent trading will test longer-duration demand after the strong three-year sale and Amazon's price-sensitive book.

The RBNZ decision follows at 22:00 ET July 7. China's June consumer and producer prices arrive July 8 at 21:30, and Japan's regional assessment and roughly ¥2.5 trillion five-year auction follow during Tokyo trading July 9. Price data and actual bids will provide a firmer basis for comparing policy paths than assuming every market must follow the US selloff.
